title: Complaint and Reference of TE Mark Herzor and TE Erwin Morrison vs. Philadelphia Presbytery
disposition_detail: On motion, Case 2002-18 (TE Erwin Morrison v. Philadelphia Presbytery, A Complaint) was found judicially out of order because it was filed against actions of a judicial commission and not the completed actions of the Presbytery (BCO 15-3, 43-1). Approved by the full SJC on October 16, 2003. Manual §10.2(b)-(d) describes a possible recommendation to dismiss if the case cannot be put in order, but the excerpt does not state that a dismissal occurred.
first_summary: Case 2002-18 was a complaint by TE Erwin Morrison against Philadelphia Presbytery. The SJC found it judicially out of order because it challenged actions of a judicial commission rather than completed Presbytery actions (BCO 15-3, 43-1). The full Commission approved the ruling on October 16, 2003. The excerpt does not state a later dismissal or merits ruling, though the SJC Manual describes a dismissal path for cases not put in order.
